title: Microsoft Purview: Purview SDK built into Microsoft Agent Framework for custom agents
summary: The briefing passes: the control commands, portal path, licensing requirements and rollout pause are supported by the checked sources. One billing-setup instruction in the checklist has no corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to embed the Purview SDK in the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK for custom agents.
claims.quote: Purview SDK embedded in Agent Framework SDK enables developers to seamlessly integrate enterprise-grade security, compliance, and governance into the AI agents they build.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Developers can attach Purview policy middleware that intercepts prompts and responses and checks configured Purview policies.
claims.quote: In your agent's workflow middleware pipeline, you can add Microsoft Purview policy middleware to intercept prompts and responses to determine if they meet the policies set up in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Learn documents a Python version of the integration.
claims.quote: from agent_framework.microsoft import PurviewPolicyMiddleware, PurviewSettings

claims.claim: Learn documents a .NET version of the integration.
claims.quote: .WithPurview(browserCredential, new PurviewSettings("My Secure Agent"))

claims.claim: The integration supports inline blocking of sensitive content using DLP policies.
claims.quote: Prevent sensitive data leaks: Inline blocking of sensitive content based on Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; front matter: licensing
claims.claim: Managing Entra-registered AI interactions with Purview requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Managing these AI interactions with Microsoft Purview requires you to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Integrated applications send prompts and responses to Purview for policy evaluation.
claims.quote: Process content: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation and returns policy actions your app must enforce (such as blocking or detecting policy modifications).

claims.claim: Members of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group can display captured prompts and responses in activity explorer.
claims.quote: Drill down to each activity to view details that include displaying the prompts and response when you're a member of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group.

claims.claim: Python policy evaluation fails closed if the middleware cannot resolve a user ID, tenant or application location.
claims.quote: Policy evaluation fails closed when the middleware can't resolve a user ID, tenant, or application location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Python ignore_exceptions setting bypasses enforcement for every error.
claims.quote: Set ignore_exceptions only when you deliberately prefer availability over enforcement; this setting bypasses enforcement for every error.

claims.claim: The Python documentation advises deriving identity from a validated server-side token rather than caller-controlled message fields.
claims.quote: Derive identity from a validated server-side token rather than caller-controlled message fields.

claims.claim: Agent middleware evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.
claims.quote: Evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.

claims.claim: Agent middleware does not evaluate a model tool call before the tool runs.
claims.quote: Doesn't evaluate context-provider output or a model tool call before the tool runs.

claims.claim: Chat middleware evaluates model tool calls before execution.
claims.quote: Evaluates context-provider output, replayed history, and model tool calls before execution. Tool results are evaluated on the next model call.

claims.claim: Chat middleware is the documented choice when policy must cover the complete model request.
claims.quote: Use PurviewChatPolicyMiddleware for data loss prevention when policy must cover the complete model request.

claims.claim: Both Python middleware types buffer a streamed response fully before releasing any update.
claims.quote: Both middleware types buffer a streamed response in full and evaluate it before releasing any update. Streaming therefore doesn't deliver content incrementally while Purview middleware is attached.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Purview portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered apps; PowerShell is required.
claims.quote: To create a DLP policy that applies to your Entra-registered app, you must use the New-DlpComplianceRule PowerShell cmdlet. The Microsoft Purview portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.

claims.claim: Documented DLP support for these apps blocks prompts based on sensitive information types and is app-scoped.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types. This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited Learn pages quote no rate for this integration and the billing page points readers to Azure pricing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Agent Framework SDK spending cap billing limit. Read all seven cited Learn pages, including the billing models table and Cost estimator tools links to Azure pricing and calculator; no integration rate is quoted in those pages.

claims.claim: The cited pages state no spending cap for this integration.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Agent Framework SDK spending cap billing limit. Read the cited middleware, billing models, Entra AI apps, developer configuration, API tutorial and cmdlet pages; no spending cap for this integration was stated.

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call can create a sensitive-information rule blocking UploadText under an existing app policy.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "Test Entra Rule" -Policy "Test Entra DLP" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true -GenerateIncidentReport @("siteadmin") -NotifyUser @("admin@contonso.onmicrosoft.com") -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.claim: Example 4 in the linked New-DlpComplianceRule reference shows creation of the prerequisite policy before its rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")

claims.claim: The printed Set-FeatureConfiguration call sets ingestion off for the named existing collection policy.
claims.quote: Set-FeatureConfiguration "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -ScenarioConfig '{"Activities": ["UploadText", "DownloadText"], "EnforcementPlanes": ["Application"], "SensitiveTypeIds": ["All"], "IsIngestionEnabled": false}'

claims.claim: New-FeatureConfiguration creates the collection policy rather than modifying an existing one.
claims.quote: New-FeatureConfiguration -FeatureScenario KnowYourData -Name "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -Mode Enable

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to check has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Confirm pay-as-you-go billing is set up and budgeted against an Azure subscription before the middleware is deployed." The table contains only a DLP rule and a collection policy, with no billing-enablement row.
